matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Before exploring any stick move, calculate the integer values of both sides of the equation and determine the numeric difference needed to achieve equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after reading the equation, before generating any candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Changing a stick without first knowing that the left side is 9 and the right side is 26, so the move cannot close the 17‑unit gap.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Systematically enumerate every way a single matchstick can be moved, considering all characters (numerals and operators) as possible sources and all positions—including creating a new character—as possible targets.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the numeric discrepancy, generate the full set of candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Only looking at moves from numerals and ignoring the possibility of moving a stick from the '+' operator.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, determine how the move changes the numeric value of the affected numeral(s) or the sign of an operator, and keep only moves that can bridge the previously computed discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating each candidate transformation generated in the previous step.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick that changes 'XVII' to 'XVI' (value –1) when the required change is +5, so the move cannot solve the puzzle.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via equals
matchstick.principle: Treat the '=' sign as two horizontal sticks; moving one of its sticks can turn it into a '-' sign, and adding a horizontal stick to a '-' can restore '='.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy suggests flipping the equality sign to subtraction or vice versa.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to another character but forgetting that the remaining single horizontal must still be a valid '-' operator.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a '-' sign, and the removed vertical can be used elsewhere (e.g., to create an 'I').
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the needed numeric adjustment involves changing addition to subtraction or adding a vertical stick to a numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from '+' but leaving the resulting '-' unused, resulting in an incomplete move.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from one character to another, ensure that after removal the source character remains a valid Roman numeral or operator, and after addition the target character (or new character) is also valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During the evaluation of each candidate transformation.
matchstick.example: Taking the only stick from an 'I' and placing it elsewhere, which leaves the source empty and invalid.

matchstick.title: Source character must stay valid after stick removal
matchstick.principle: Before moving a stick, verify that the character you are taking it from can lose that stick and still represent a legal Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During candidate generation for any stick move.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from an 'X' and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: X↔V intra‑character transformation
matchstick.principle: When an X (two crossing diagonals) or V (two angled sticks) appears, consider moving one diagonal/angled stick within the same character to turn X into V (or V into X), changing its value by ±5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the numeric discrepancy is a multiple of 5 and the equation contains an X or V.
matchstick.example: Ignoring the possibility of turning an X into a V, which could reduce the value by 5 and solve the puzzle.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved directly from one operator to another, simultaneously changing both operators (e.g., turning '=' into '-' while turning '-' into '=', by swapping a horizontal stick).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy suggests swapping the roles of two operators.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' but not checking that the resulting operators are both valid.

matchstick.title: Form new numeral by adding stick
matchstick.principle: When relocating a stick to a new position, consider that the stick may constitute a standalone numeral (e.g., a vertical stick becomes an 'I') or extend an existing numeral; verify that the resulting character(s) are valid Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During inter‑character relocation, especially when the target location is empty or adjacent to other numerals.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from '+' to a blank spot but failing to recognize that it can form a new 'I', thus missing a valid solution.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character without checking whether the remaining strokes still form a legal Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always verify that the source character can lose the chosen stick and still be a valid symbol before committing to the move.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes a move will fix the equation without recomputing the numeric values of both sides.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each candidate move, recalculate the values of both sides and confirm that they are equal before accepting the transformation.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: In an attempt to simplify the puzzle, the model deletes characters or operators, breaking the required equation structure.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Maintain the full sequence of numerals, operators, and the equality sign; only relocate sticks, never delete characters.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model changes an operator (e.g., '+' to '-') but does not account for how the sign change alters the arithmetic result.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When an operator is modified, recompute the expression using the new operator to see its effect on the overall numeric balance.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model returns the original equation unchanged, violating the rule that exactly one stick must be relocated.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that the final answer reflects a single stick relocation; explicitly note the changed character(s) in the solution.
